idiom_name: companion object factory functions + require() preconditions
implementation_notes: Kotlin documents companion objects explicitly as the place for factory methods, so the creation owner is companion object { fun fromCart(...) } on the aggregate, optionally with operator fun invoke so the primary path reads as Order(...); the classic factory class is unnecessary. Validation happens in init blocks or through require()/check() preconditions, which makes an invalid instance unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. Use a sealed interface/class when the factory must decide which subtype to return (the caller then gets an exhaustive when), and return Result or a domain error when construction failure is an expected outcome instead of an exception.
pitfalls: copy() on a data class is generated even for a private constructor and bypasses require() checks; use a regular class when the factory must be the only door.
require()/check() throw IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException - right for programmer errors, wrong for invalid user or persisted input, which deserves Result or a typed error.
A companion object is initialized lazily and thread-safely, but mutable factory state (a creator registry) is shared across threads; keep it immutable or synchronize it.
